stem: An insurance firm keeps its 2,000 employees in an external SAML 2.0 identity provider and has 12 AWS accounts in one organization. Employees must use their existing corporate sign-in to reach every account they are entitled to from one portal, and the identity team wants to manage only one federation trust. What should a solutions architect recommend?

choices.text: Enable IAM Identity Center, connect the IdP as its identity source, and assign groups to accounts with permission sets
Create an Amazon Cognito user pool federated with the IdP and map its groups to IAM roles in each of the 12 accounts
Add the IdP as an IAM SAML identity provider in each of the 12 accounts and create federated roles in every account
Enable an account instance of IAM Identity Center in one of the 12 member accounts and assign permission sets from there

rationale: IAM Identity Center provides one point of federation with a single SAML certificate to manage, an AWS access portal where users see all of their assigned accounts, and permission sets that it provisions as roles in each account. Amazon Cognito is an identity platform for users of your web and mobile apps; it is not the service for workforce sign-in to AWS accounts. Per-account IAM SAML federation works, but the SAML provider used in a role trust policy must be in the same account as the role, so the team would maintain 12 separate trusts. Account instances support only application assignments; multi-account permissions and portal access to AWS accounts need an organization instance.
